instruction: Adjust cell dimensions in this attendance tracking spreadsheet to ensure all data fits on one page when exported to PDF. Save the PDF with the same name as the spreadsheet in the home folder.

metadata.explanation: Attendance tracking context. Single-page PDF verification with content validation.
metadata.verification_details: Uses existing check_pdf_pages metric to verify: (1) PDF file exists at /home/user/Resize_Cells_Fit_Page.pdf, (2) PDF has exactly 1 page (relation=eq, ref_value=1), (3) PDF file size > 10KB (verify_content=True). No custom functions needed as check_pdf_pages is already available in desktop_env.evaluators.metrics.pdf.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical semantic issue: verify_content=true checks for images in PDF (lines 46-58 in pdf.py), but LibreOffice Calc spreadsheets export as text/vector graphics, not raster images
The image verification logic will cause false negatives for normal spreadsheet-to-PDF exports, making the evaluator unable to verify correctly completed tasks
The evaluator correctly checks page count (1 page) and file existence, which aligns with instruction requirements
File size check (>10KB) is reasonable for ensuring non-empty PDF output
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Remove verify_content flag or set to false, as the page count check is sufficient to verify the instruction requirement
Alternatively, modify check_pdf_pages to have a content verification mode suitable for spreadsheet PDFs (check for text content instead of images)
Consider adding text extraction verification to confirm the PDF contains actual spreadsheet data, not just checking for images

rule_validation_issues.msg: metric check_pdf_pages first parameter type (str) may not match getter get_vm_file return type (Union)
